_meta.indication: Treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active-comparator (EU-sourced ustekinumab) controlled, parallel-group 52-week trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥ 18 years with stable moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis of ≥ 6 months duration, BSA ≥ 10%, PASI ≥ 12, sPGA ≥ 3, candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary at Week 16: proportion achieving sPGA of 0 or 1, and proportion achieving PASI 90
pivotal_trials.result: sPGA 0/1: 88% vs 8% placebo; PASI 90: 75% vs 5% placebo (p-values < 0.001)

nct_ctgov.title: BI 655066 (Risankizumab) Compared to Placebo and Active Comparator (Ustekinumab) in Patients With Moderate to Severe Chronic Plaque Psoriasis

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active-comparator (EU-sourced ustekinumab) controlled, parallel-group 52-week trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥ 18 years with stable moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis of ≥ 6 months duration, BSA ≥ 10%, PASI ≥ 12, sPGA ≥ 3, candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary at Week 16: proportion achieving sPGA of 0 or 1, and proportion achieving PASI 90
pivotal_trials.result: sPGA 0/1: 84% vs 5% placebo; PASI 90: 75% vs 2% placebo (p-values < 0.001)

nct_ctgov.title: BI 655066 Versus Placebo & Active Comparator (Ustekinumab) in Patients With Moderate to Severe Chronic Plaque Psoriasis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 1%): upper respiratory infections (13.0% vs 9.7% placebo), headache (3.5% vs 2.0%), fatigue (2.5% vs 1.0%), injection site reactions (1.5% vs 1.0%), and tinea infections (1.1% vs 0.3%). Infections occurred in 22.1% of SKYRIZI vs 14.7% of placebo through 16 weeks.
target_moa: Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the p19 subunit of IL-23 and inhibits its interaction with the IL-23 receptor, blocking IL-23-driven inflammatory responses that contribute to plaque psoriasis

rems.type: A Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is not needed

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held; the safety profile was expected to be comparable to other biologics for this indication and there were no novel or complex regulatory issues requiring public discussion

summary.text: SKYRIZI (risankizumab) BLA 761105 received a Standard review (received 4/23/2018, PDUFA goal 4/23/2019) and was approved on the traditional pathway based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials; no Advisory Committee meeting was held and no accelerated-approval, breakthrough, orphan, or priority-review designations were applied.

citations.quote:
Priority or Standard	Standard
Submit Date(s)	4/23/2018
Received Date(s)	4/23/2018
PDUFA Goal Date	4/23/2019

The applicant submitted data from two adequate and well-controlled [trials M15-995 (1311.28), M16-008 (1311.3)], which provided evidence of the effectiveness of risankizumab for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.
The Agency held no Advisory Committee Meeting regarding this application because the safety profile was expected to be comparable to that of other biologic products approved for this indication.

requirement.text: 3594-1: Deferred pediatric study – conduct a PK, safety and efficacy study in pediatric subjects 6 to <18 years of age with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (with at least one year risankizumab exposure)

citations.quote: 3594 – 1 Conduct a pharmacokinetics (PK), safety and efficacy study in pediatric subjects 6 to <18 years of age with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (with a duration of exposure to risankizumab of at least one year).

requirement.text: 3594-2: Prospective, registry-based observational exposure cohort study comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to risankizumab during pregnancy to an unexposed control population

citations.quote: 3594– 2 A prospective, registry based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to risankizumab during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3594-3: Retrospective cohort study (claims/EMR) or case-control study to assess adverse pregnancy outcomes in women exposed to risankizumab during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population

citations.quote: 3594 – 3 Conduct a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study to assess adverse pregnancy outcomes such as major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age, neonatal deaths, and infant infections in women exposed to risankizumab during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3594-4: Observational study to assess long-term safety of risankizumab compared to other therapies in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, with long-term malignancy as the primary outcome

citations.quote: 3594 – 4 Conduct an observational study to assess the long-term safety of risankizumab compared to other therapies used in the treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy in the course of actual clinical care. The study's primary outcome is long-term malignancy.
